title: Choosing a model per decision: one audited switch, the rule as the fallback, demotion below the bar
request: For each decision point, the answerers that passed their gates ranked; routing that picks one with a reviewer and a reason; the rule as the fallback when a model abstains or fails; demotion when its accuracy on new labels falls below its bar. Done when switching a point's model is one audited change and a demoted model falls back to the rule.
spec: A decisions section in the workspace's routing document, a switch that audits every change, an answer function that falls back to the rule, a demotion that reads new labels, and two routes.
plan: Read the model purposes' routing and its audit pattern.
Write the decision routing beside it, the answer function and the demotion.
Add the routes and their permission.

decisions.decision: Decision routing lives in the same routing document as the model purposes.
decisions.why: One store and one history per workspace, on files and PostgreSQL, with no new table.

decisions.decision: To act, a model needs its sealed gate and a shadow measurement at least as right as the rule.
decisions.why: A gate on generated tables did not carry over to the studio's decisions in 22.4.

decisions.decision: Act with a check holds a disagreement for a person; only act uses the model alone.
decisions.why: Two levels that behave alike are one level.

decisions.decision: A demotion is DCLab's own change in the audit trail.
decisions.why: Writing it as a reviewer's would name a person who never made it.

change: dclab_rnd/ledger/routing.py (new), agentic/pages/ledger.py (routing routes; a demotion check when a blind label arrives), accounts/guard.py, audit.py (the backfill reads decision changes), the web client; tests/test_decision_routing.py (new), test_experience_log.py; the plan, the roadmap, CLAUDE.md.

findings.scenario: The client test failed because the new routes were not in it.
findings.cause: The frontend was not rebuilt after the routes were added.

findings.defect: Demotion counted blind labels without their weights.
findings.scenario: 90 agreeing decisions drawn at 0.1 and 60 differing ones at 0.6: a weighted accuracy of 0.96 was counted as 0.84 and the model demoted.
findings.fix: A blind label weighs as it was drawn.

findings.defect: A model could be promoted to act without any shadow evidence.
findings.scenario: The leakage classifier, right on 2 of 11 labelled disagreements, could be set to act.
findings.cause: Only the sealed gate was checked.
findings.fix: To act, at least 20 labelled disagreements in shadow and a weighted accuracy on them at least the rule's.

findings.defect: Act with a check behaved like act.
findings.scenario: At level 2 a model saying yes against the rule's no was used.
findings.fix: At level 2 a disagreement keeps the rule's value and holds the decision for a person.

findings.defect: An automatic demotion was written as a reviewer's.
findings.scenario: The audit row named a human reviewer, and under accounts the person who gave the blind label.
findings.cause: The demotion called the person's switch.
findings.fix: The demotion is written as DCLab's own change.

findings.defect: With no rule the answer listed None and said the rule was used, and a refused value could be used.
findings.scenario: No rule gave a list holding None; a model value outside the point's answers was acted on.
findings.fix: Only real answers are listed, used is none without a rule, and a refused value falls back.

findings.defect: The ranking promised speed and guessed the cost.
findings.scenario: Speed was never measured and cost came from the answerer's name.
findings.fix: The ranking says what it uses, with the weighted shadow figure; speed is said to be unmeasured.

findings.defect: Every blind label read the whole ledger, and a failed check failed the label.
findings.scenario: A large workspace paid for a full read on each label; an error after the label was saved answered 500.
findings.cause: The check ran unconditionally and unguarded.
findings.fix: Only a label at a routed point runs the check, on that point's decisions, and a failure never fails the label.

findings.defect: Two writers could lose a change to the shared routing document.
findings.scenario: A model routing change and a decision routing change at once.
findings.cause: Read, change and write of the whole document.
findings.fix: A lock within the process; across processes it is said to remain open.

findings.defect: The audit backfill read a decision change as a model change.
findings.scenario: After a migration a decision change would show as set_routing with no purpose.
findings.cause: The backfill knew one kind of entry.
findings.fix: A decision change is backfilled as one, with its point.

findings.defect: A bar change left no trace, and a bar of 0 became 0.9.
findings.scenario: The audit row's from and to omitted the bar; a zero bar was silently replaced.
findings.cause: The bar was not in the change and a falsy value took the default.
findings.fix: The bar is in from and to, and a bar outside 0.5 to 1 is refused.

measurements.name: planted faults
measurements.gate: each planted fault fails a test

outcome: Each decision point's answerer is changed by one audited switch, acts only after its sealed gate and a shadow measurement at least as right as the rule, falls back to the rule when it abstains, fails or disagrees at a check, and is demoted by DCLab below its bar.
lessons: Weigh a sampled label by how it was drawn whenever it decides something.
Two levels with one behaviour are one level: make each level do what its name says.
Write an automatic action as the system's, never as a person's.
risks: Nothing in the studio asks the routing yet (22.9).
Across processes the routing document can still lose a concurrent change.
